title: Engineering Manager
description:
🏆 What's the opportunity?

Air freight carries less than 1% of world trade by volume and more than a third of it by value, around $22.7 billion of goods every single day. It's how a vaccine reaches a clinic before it spoils, how a semiconductor arrives before the production line stops, and how a retailer restocks a continent away in three days instead of five weeks. When speed is the whole point, freight flies.

Somebody has to price it, book it and move it, and that work is still done largely by hand, in inboxes and spreadsheets.

For eight years we've been building the data infrastructure underneath it: direct integrations with 75 airlines, the top ten ocean carriers and dozens of GSAs, used every day by 30,000 freight forwarders across 172 countries to hold their rates, price their business and book their freight.

In 2026 we acquired Cargofive, and cargo.one now spans air and ocean, the two modes that carry international trade. That foundation is what makes the next part possible.

In March 2026 we launched the industry's first AI-native operating system for multimodal freight:one workspace where freight teams and AI agents work side by side across rate management, procurement, quoting, booking and support. Crane Worldwide and Yusen Logistics are rolling it out across their global operations.

AI-led engineering is how we build. Engineers write specs and acceptance criteria, agents do much of the implementation, and the engineer owns the architecture, the review and what ships.

We're backed by Index Ventures, Bessemer, Creandum, Point Nine, Next47 and Lufthansa Cargo, which has been an investor in us since 2018.

🚀 What makes this role different

This is an engineering management job for a team where agents do much of the implementation. That changes the job.

When producing code gets cheaper and faster, the bottleneck moves. Throughput depends more on how well engineers define the problem, direct the agents, review what comes back and tell a plausible answer from a correct one.

You'll lead our engineers: what they ship, how good it is, how fast they move, whether the people are growing, and how quickly the team gets better at working AI-led. A lot of what engineering managers know about pacing, estimating, reviewing and measuring a team was calibrated for a different bottleneck. Working out what good looks like now is part of this job.

Today, engineers direct agents on their own work. That's where we are, but it's not the end state. We're building toward fleets of agents that work on their own inside guardrails and harnesses we design, while engineers move up to setting direction, reviewing what comes back, and owning what ships. Part of your job is helping the team get there while keeping the quality bar high.

This is also a player-coach role. You'll stay close enough to the code to keep your judgment sharp and your technical credibility current, while the engineers you lead and what they deliver remain the focus.

🧭 What we're looking for — the part that isn't negotiable

You get more from growing people than from being the smartest person in the room. You've watched someone you managed become better than you at something and enjoyed it. You run real one-to-ones, not status meetings. You give hard feedback early and kindly, and you've done the hard version more than once.

You think in systems. Teams are systems too. You can see why delivery is slipping without needing someone to tell you, and you fix the process rather than working harder inside a broken one.

You're excited about the business. You want to know what your engineers' work is worth and what it does for the customer paying us. You can explain that to them so their work has a point beyond the issue they're closing.

You work at eye level with Product. You co-own what gets built and when, push back on the brief, and don't treat "Product decides, Engineering delivers" as a healthy way to work.

You want to be in the room with customers. Freight forwarders and airlines, directly. You'd rather hear the problem first-hand, and you take your engineers with you.

English is your working language, at close to native fluency. You write and speak it the way you think in it. Almost everything a manager does in a remote-first company is language: the feedback that has to land precisely, the written decision that stops a debate, the difficult conversation where the wrong word costs you trust.

You'll also need:

  • Experience managing engineers: hiring them, growing them, running performance honestly and shipping on a predictable cadence.

  • A backend engineering background, strong architecture instincts and enough technical currency that your engineers respect your technical opinion.

  • A delivery track record. Specific things that shipped, on a schedule you can describe, and an honest account of what slipped and why.

  • Experience building a team, not only running one. You know how to assess for potential, close a candidate and set someone up so their first ninety days work.

  • Genuine engagement with AI-led engineering. You don't need to be an expert, but you can't manage engineers working this way from the outside. You need to use the tools yourself and want to get good at them.

  • Judgment, and the nerve to use it. You'll make calls with incomplete information and own them out loud.

  • Low ego. You take feedback from your own engineers and change your mind in public.

Nice to have: experience with our stack of Python 3, Flask, gRPC, PostgreSQL, Redis, Celery and Kubernetes on GCP; Vue.js; managing a distributed team across several countries; or introducing a new way of working to a team that didn't ask for one.

🎬 A snapshot of what you'll be doing

  • Own delivery. What ships, how good it is and whether the commitments you make hold.

  • Grow the people. One-to-ones that are worth the hour, honest performance conversations, career paths that mean something, and knowing what each person wants next.

  • Hire. You'll own the hiring bar and run your own loops. We hire senior engineers on judgement and character rather than AI experience, and teach them the workflow. You'll be central to making that work.

  • Partner with Product as an equal. Shape the roadmap, negotiate scope and protect engineers from churn that isn't worth it.

  • Raise the team's AI capability. Help engineers use agents better today, spread what works, remove friction, and help evolve our setup toward autonomous agent fleets with the right guardrails and harnesses in place.

  • Stay technical, roughly a day a week. Reviews, a well-chosen piece of work, enough to keep your hands and judgement in.

  • Go to the users. Sit with freight forwarders and airlines, and take your engineers with you.

🤖 What you'd be working with

We're honest about where we are: Everything below is real and running today, but some of it is young, adoption is uneven across our five teams, and the next stage doesn't exist yet. You'd help build it, not inherit it.

How we work AI-led:

  • Work starts from a spec: Tickets and specs are drafted with agent help, against our agreed templates. Once a spec meets the bar, engineers pick it up, refine it, and own the design and architecture decisions; only then do agents start implementing.

  • Conventions for how agents get context, how work runs in parallel, and how the results come back together safely.

  • AI review on every merge request in CI, and a human review standard built for telling a plausible answer from a correct one.

What we've built to make that work:

  • Our shared AI engineering practice: spec templates, a directory of reusable AI skills, agent harnesses and review conventions for giving agents context, running work in parallel and bringing the results back together safely.

  • A Slack-triggered agent (Timber) that takes a Jira ticket and delivers a merge request, currently handling all bugs and small, well-scoped tickets and built on our RAG context layer and a memory layer.

  • A triage agent that protects the team's focus: it routes incoming questions, tickets and reports from other internal teams to the right engineering team and does the first level of triage itself; answering directly, creating a bug ticket, or escalating to a human.

The furthest edge of this is our AI team's production work, the bar the rest of the practice is being pulled toward, and closing that gap across the department is part of your job:

  • AI doing commercial work in production. In June 2026, Saudia Cargo went live with an AI worker our engineers built. It handles inbound rate requests around the clock and returns a quote in seconds, cutting turnaround time by 68% with 89% first-time accuracy.

  • An LLM pipeline turning airlines' free-text email replies into structured, bookable quotes.

❤️ How we work

  • Feedback is constant and direct, in both directions. You'll get it in your first week and you're expected to give it.

  • Remote-first, which means we write things down.

  • You take ownership, and you back your opinions with data.

  • Given the ambitious option and the easy one, you take the ambitious one.

  • Diverse, and playful about it.

✨ What we offer

  • Equity in cargo.one. This role is equity-eligible.

  • Company-provided Claude Code and the other AI tools the work requires.

  • A one-time €650 home office budget, plus your choice of MacBook or Dell laptop, delivered before day one.

  • Co-working access through our partner Desana.

  • 24 paid vacation days on top of your country's public holidays, plus special leave.

  • Two company-wide offsites a year, plus team trips.

  • Permanent full-time employment. In Germany, a contract with cargo.one. In Portugal, a contract with our subsidiary Cargo Five. Elsewhere in our approved hiring countries, through our partner Remote.com.

🌍 Where you'll work

We're remote across our approved hiring countries in the European timezone band, so the engineering team overlaps for most of the working day.

We currently hire in:

Armenia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czechia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Georgia, Germany, Greece, Hungary, Ireland, Kosovo, Latvia, Lithuania, Malta, Moldova, Norway, Poland, Portugal, Romania, Serbia, Slovakia, South Africa, Spain, Sweden, Ukraine and the United Kingdom.

We meet in person regularly, including twice a year as a full company.

We can currently support visa processes in Germany only.

We hire for talent. If you don't tick every box but think you'd be a great match, reach out anyway. We'd love to hear from you.

At Nomos, we care about our craft and take full responsibility for what we build. We hire for spikes, not an absence of weaknesses, and look for exceptional ability backed by a record of achievement. What you’ll do

We’re building an energy company from first principles. That means rethinking the operational work behind it: which processes we need, how they run, and what agents can take on. You’ll build the AI systems that let Nomos serve more customers without scaling manual work at the same rate.

  • Work directly with customers and internal teams to understand their workflows and find where AI can make the biggest difference.

  • Build agents and integrations that handle real operational work, from customer onboarding to communication with energy market participants.

Exciting challenges

  • Rethink how an energy company operates. Building from scratch gives us the freedom to question processes that established suppliers take for granted. You’ll decide how software, agents, and people work together and turn that into systems the company depends on every day.

  • Put the newest AI capabilities to work in production. Nomos is built around AI. You’ll have access to new models and tools as they become available, with generous spending limits to experiment. The engineering challenge is making them dependable at scale: testing behaviour, handling exceptions, and knowing when a person needs to step in.

 

Who you are

  • You’ve shipped and operated production software. You understand how systems fit together, how they fail, and how to keep them working as usage grows.

  • You have hands-on experience building with AI. You can connect models to tools and data, evaluate their behaviour, and make sound decisions about where agents are useful.

  • You move quickly and care about the details. You turn an ambiguous problem into working software, test it properly, and stay responsible for it after launch.

 

References

Paul Burkhardt

 

Why join us?

As an early member of Nomos, you’ll help shape the company and share in its financial upside. Backed by Index Ventures, we’re building a European category leader in one of the world’s largest industries, making electricity affordable and Europe more competitive.

Building a power company from scratch brings complex, rewarding challenges and the chance to solve Europe’s energy crisis for the long term. You’ll learn from people with exceptional depth in their fields, challenge each other’s thinking and take responsibility from the start.

title: Senior Software Engineer - Cloud Partner Integrations
description:
About the team

Most providers make customers migrate their data to them. We're doing the opposite: bringing ClickHouse Cloud into the environments our customers already trust, so their data stays useful right where it lives.

Those environments come in a few shapes. Some are major cloud data platforms that run ClickHouse as a native service, so customers get it without leaving the tool they already use. Some are BI and visualization tools that need ClickHouse to show up as a fast, first-class data source behind their dashboards. And some are developer and data platforms we connect through marketplaces and identity federation with a couple of clicks to link an account. The goal is the same every time: ClickHouse should feel like a first-class citizen in every environment.

As the founding backend engineer, you'll set the technical defaults for this team. You'll have end-to-end ownership, but you'll also work inside the constraints of platforms you don't own: thin documentation, unfamiliar deployment topologies, and timelines governed by partner approval cycles. A lot of the challenge is engineering across trust boundaries you don't fully control. You won't be doing it alone. You'll work closely with the team's engineering manager and a small founding group that will grow around you, but you'll be the one setting the technical direction. If that sounds like your kind of challenge, let's talk.

What you'll do

You'll own an integration end to end: the design, the code, and the production system that keeps running after launch. You're setting the technical defaults a growing team will inherit, so the early decisions matter.

Day to day, that looks like:

  • Owning the architecture: auth and identity flows, multi-tenancy, how data moves and where it's allowed to live, performance, and what happens in production

  • Running what you build. You'll be on-call for your own work from early on, before there's a dedicated platform to lean on, which means owning the infrastructure, CI, deployment, and observability behind it

  • Working on top of external platforms you can't change, and being straight about which risks are yours to manage and which aren't

  • Partnering closely with the internal teams whose services you depend on: asking clearly, agreeing on interfaces, and finding ways to keep moving instead of waiting around to be unblocked

  • You've worked with modern auth protocols, service principals, and identity federation, and you know how to get it right across a trust boundary

title: Product Designer - Germany (m/w/d)
description:
Möchtest du das Leben von Millionen Unternehmer in Europa verändern?

Du möchtest echten Impact haben und die Zukunft von Finanzen und Buchhaltung in Europa mitgestalten? Du fühlst dich in einem dynamischen Umfeld wohl, das auf Vertrauen, Eigenverantwortung und Geschwindigkeit setzt? Und unsere Design-Prinzipien entsprechen deiner Vorstellung von großartigen Nutzererlebnissen?

Dann könnte Pennylane genau der richtige Ort für dich sein – und du genau die richtige Person für diese Rolle.

Unsere Vision

Wir bauen das beliebteste Financial Operating System für kleine und mittelständische Unternehmen in Europa.

Unser Ziel ist es, Unternehmer von zeitaufwendigen Aufgaben rund um Buchhaltung und Finanzen zu entlasten und ihnen gleichzeitig Zugang zu den wichtigsten Finanzinformationen zu geben, damit sie bessere Entscheidungen für ihr Unternehmen treffen können.

Gleichzeitig unterstützen wir Steuerkanzleien dabei, weniger Zeit für repetitive Aufgaben aufzuwenden und sich stärker auf die Beratung und Betreuung ihrer Mandant zu konzentrieren.

Bereits heute nutzen mehr als 1.000.000 kleine und mittelständische Unternehmen sowie über 6.500 Steuerkanzleien Pennylane in Frankreich.

Über uns

Pennylane gehört zu den am schnellsten wachsenden FinTechs in Frankreich – und bald auch in Deutschland.

In nur fünf Jahren haben wir:

  • uns als innovative Accounting- und Finanzplattform für Unternehmen und Steuerkanzleien etabliert,

  • insgesamt 150 Millionen Euro Kapital eingesammelt – unter anderem von Sequoia, dem renommierten Silicon-Valley-Investor hinter Unternehmen wie Google, Facebook, Airbnb, Stripe und PayPal,

  • unser Team von 7 Gründer auf über 1.100 Pennylaners ausgebaut,

  • eine internationale Unternehmenskultur mit mehr als 25 Nationalitäten geschaffen,

  • eine starke Remote-First-Kultur etabliert, in der bereits rund 30 % unserer Mitarbeitenden von überall in Europa arbeiten,

  • das Vertrauen tausender Kund und Steuerkanzleien gewonnen und hervorragende Bewertungen erhalten.

Heute gelten wir mit einer Glassdoor-Bewertung von 4,6/5 als einer der attraktivsten Arbeitgeber Europas.

Pennylane Deutschland

Innerhalb von nur 1,5 Jahren ist unser Deutschland-Team von einer einzelnen Squad auf über 40 Mitarbeitende in den Bereichen Product, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success und Marketing gewachsen.

Unser Ziel ist es, Pennylane als festen Bestandteil des deutschen Marktes zu etablieren. Gemeinsam mit innovativen Steuerberater und Unternehmen entwickeln wir unser Produkt für die Anforderungen des deutschen Marktes weiter und verändern nachhaltig die Art und Weise, wie Buchhaltung und Finanzen in Deutschland funktionieren.

Als eigenständiger Markt profitieren wir von der Unterstützung unserer französischen Teams und genießen gleichzeitig große Freiheiten bei der Gestaltung unserer Ziele, Strukturen, Prozesse und Produkte.

Design bei Pennylane

Design steht im Zentrum unserer Mission. Unser Anspruch ist es, Nutzer ein nahtloses, zugängliches und begeisterndes Produkterlebnis zu bieten.

Unser Design-Team besteht aus über 40 Product Designer, die in interdisziplinären Squads eng mit Product und Engineering zusammenarbeiten.

Autonomie, Vertrauen und Transparenz bilden das Fundament unserer Unternehmenskultur und prägen den Arbeitsalltag unserer Designer.

Bei Pennylane beschränkt sich Design nicht auf die Gestaltung von Interfaces. Designer begleiten den gesamten Prozess – von der Definition des Problems über Research und Testing bis hin zur Umsetzung der Lösung.

Deine Rolle

Wir suchen eine Product Designer mit fundierter Erfahrung im B2B-Produktdesign, um die Weiterentwicklung unseres Produkts in Deutschland aktiv mitzugestalten.

Wenn du gerne reale Nutzerprobleme löst, in einem kollaborativen Umfeld arbeitest und ein echtes Interesse daran hast, Nutzerverhalten und Geschäftsziele zu verstehen, wirst du bei Pennylane viele Gleichgesinnte finden.

Das bringst du mit

  • Du verstehst sowohl Nutzerbedürfnisse als auch Business-Anforderungen und kannst Erkenntnisse aus User Research, Marktanalysen und Daten in pragmatische Lösungen übersetzen.

  • Du hast Erfahrung mit komplexen digitalen Produkten und Systemen, beispielsweise mit mehreren Modulen, umfangreichen Funktionen oder komplexen Datenstrukturen.

  • Du arbeitest eng mit Entwickler, Product Manager und weiteren Stakeholdern wie Sales oder Support zusammen und kannst technische Rahmenbedingungen sowie Business-Ziele in deine Arbeit integrieren.

  • Du kommunizierst klar, hinterfragst bestehende Annahmen konstruktiv und kannst deine Lösungsansätze überzeugend vertreten.

  • Du sprichst fließend Deutsch und Englisch. User Interviews werden regelmäßig auf Deutsch durchgeführt.

Was dich bei Pennylane erwartet

Innerhalb des ersten Monats

  • Du lernst unser Unternehmen, unsere Teams und unsere Vision während des Onboardings kennen.

  • Du erhältst einen tiefen Einblick in unser Produkt sowie die Welt der Buchhaltung und Finanzen.

  • Du machst dich mit unserer Product- und Design-Organisation, unseren Methoden und unserer Kultur vertraut.

  • Du lernst die Menschen kennen, mit denen du täglich zusammenarbeiten wirst – sowohl innerhalb des Deutschland-Teams als auch im internationalen Umfeld.

Innerhalb der ersten drei Monate

  • Du führst Discovery-Workshops und User Research durch und analysierst Daten, Nutzerfeedback und Business-Anforderungen.

  • Gemeinsam mit deinem Product Manager verantwortest du die kontinuierliche Weiterentwicklung deines Produktbereichs.

  • Du entwickelst Lösungen in der passenden Detailtiefe – von ersten Konzepten bis hin zu High-Fidelity-Prototypen.

  • Du bringst deine Erfahrung aktiv ins Team ein, gibst Feedback an Kolleg und arbeitest an bereichsübergreifenden Themen mit.

Innerhalb der ersten sechs Monate

  • Du unterstützt aktiv beim Ausbau unseres Teams und wirkst im Recruiting-Prozess mit.

  • Du beobachtest aktuelle UX- und UI-Trends und bringst Best Practices aus der internationalen Tech-Welt ein.

Und darüber hinaus

Sowohl unser Design-Team als auch unsere Aktivitäten in Deutschland werden weiter wachsen.

Das bedeutet für dich:

  • Möglichkeiten, neue Designer einzustellen, zu coachen und perspektivisch zu führen.

  • Mehr Verantwortung für strategische Projekte.

  • Die Chance, Prozesse, Tools und Best Practices aktiv mitzugestalten und weiterzuentwickeln.

Das bieten wir dir

  • Arbeite aus unserem Büro im Herzen Berlins, aus unserem Standort in Hamburg, aus unseren Büros in Paris oder aus jedem WeWork-Standort in Europa.

  • Bei einem Full-Remote-Vertrag erhältst du ein Budget für dein Home Office sowie einen monatlichen Zuschuss für Coworking-Spaces.

  • Zusätzlich zu 25 Urlaubstagen erhältst du jährlich zwischen 8 und 13 weitere freie Tage.

  • Zugang zu Busuu, um dein Englisch zu verbessern oder eine neue Sprache zu lernen.

  • Modernste Apple-Hardware für deinen Arbeitsalltag.

  • Eine lebendige Community mit gemeinsamen Sportaktivitäten wie Fußball, Laufen oder Klettern.

  • Regelmäßige Team-Events, After-Work-Abende und unsere beliebten Rooftop-Drinks in Berlin.

  • Ein jährliches Company Offsite – zuletzt waren wir gemeinsam im Center Parcs und hatten eine großartige Zeit.

Unser Bewerbungsprozess

  1. Portfolio Review

  2. Erstgespräch mit Sonia oder Barbara (Technical Recruiting) – 30 Minuten

  3. Interview mit zwei Mitgliedern unseres Design-Teams – 45 bis 60 Minuten

  4. Take-Home Assessment inklusive Präsentation und Review mit zwei weiteren Designer – 60 Minuten

  5. Finales Gespräch mit unserem Chief Product Officer und dem Head of Product Germany – 60 Minuten

Vielfalt und Chancengleichheit

Bei Pennylane fördern wir Vielfalt in all ihren Formen und schaffen ein inklusives, wertschätzendes und erfüllendes Arbeitsumfeld – sowohl im Büro als auch remote.

Wir bieten allen Bewerber die gleichen Chancen – unabhängig von Herkunft, Nationalität, Geschlecht, Religion, sexueller Orientierung, Alter oder Behinderung.

title: (Senior) Software Engineer, Robot control (f/m/d)
description:
About TACTILIA:

At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI. Spun out of SCHUNK, the global market leader in gripping technology, we combine a decade of robotic-hand expertise and real industrial access with the speed and ambition of a deep-tech startup.

This isn't a research project waiting for its first customer. We already have a product, customers are ready to use it, and we are launching now. Your work will directly shape the electronics, actuators, and embedded systems that make that possible.

You will join at the moment when the hard engineering questions become real product decisions: how do we make a highly capable robotic hand reliable, manufacturable, serviceable, and simple enough to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role:

As a (Senior) Software Engineer, Robot Control at TACTILIA Robotics, you will help design and build the software that turns our robotic hardware into a reliable, scalable product.

You will work across embedded, control, and application software, taking ownership of complex technical problems and helping shape the architecture as the platform evolves. You will work closely with the CTO and engineering team, with the autonomy to make important technical decisions and see them through to working systems.

This is a hands-on role. You will move between architecture, implementation, and the lab, solving the challenges that arise when software meets real hardware

What you will do:

  • Set the architecture. Embedded, control, and application layers — modular and reusable across product variants, not a one-off for a single prototype.

  • Write the control loops that can't miss a beat. Deterministic firmware on the embedded target: hardware abstraction, sensor/actuator integration, fault handling, hard real-time constraints. No room for "usually works."

  • Turn commands into grasps. Position, torque, force impedance and admittance control, coordinated multi-finger motion, and handle all different states to make the grasp stable and reliable

  • Build the simulation before hardware pays the price Simulation models for control development, regression testing, and sim-to-real validation — most iteration should happen before anyone touches a real hand.

  • Ship SDKs people actually want to integrate. ROS 2, fieldbuses, and customer-facing interfaces — documented and version-stable, not tribal knowledge.

  • Make the sensor data mean something. Build the pipeline for tactile, position, and force data; build models for slip detection and contact-state estimation; turn field telemetry into the next product iteration.

  • Get ahead of the Cyber Resilience Act. Security by design, SBOM, vulnerability handling, a real update path — well before the December 2027 deadline, including the technical documentation for conformity assessment.

  • Build tooling like it's product, not plumbing. CI/CD, automated and simulation-based regression tests, logging and diagnostics you'd actually want to debug with at 2am.

  • Work across the whole team. Tight loop with Electronics, Mechanics, and Application —spec input, customer integration support, the works.

What you bring:

  • A degree in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Mechatronics, Robotics, or a related field.

  • 5–10 years building embedded, robotics, or control software, ideally including at least one product that reached series production or product maturity

  • Strong modern C++ and Python with a deep understanding of real-time behaviour, concurrency, memory and resource constraints

  • Solid hands-on experience with robot control: closed-loop control, state estimation, filtering, motion coordination, force/impedance control, or related areas.

  • You have architected software for a product, not a prototype someone else productionized later

  • Simulation-based development (Isaac Sim, Gazebo, MuJoCo, or similar)

  • Comfortable with Linux, Git, CI/CD, automated testing

  • A strong hardware mindset: you enjoy bringing up systems, debugging on real robots, and getting to the bottom of problems with a scope, logic analyzer, debugger, or whatever tool gets the job done

  • Fluent English; German is a plus, not a requirement

Bonus:

  • Dexterous manipulation, grasp planning, or robotic hands

  • Tactile sensing and contact-rich manipulation

title: Head of Product (f/m/d)
description:
Head of Product (f/m/d)

About TACTILIA:

At TACTILIA, we are building the industry-ready robotic hand that closes one of the biggest gaps in Physical AI. Spun out of Schunk, the global market leader in gripping technology, we combine a decade of robotic-hand expertise and real industrial access with the speed and ambition of a deep-tech startup.

This isn't a research project waiting for its first customer. We already have a product, customers are ready to use it, and we are launching now. Your work will directly shape the product, roadmap, and development process that make that possible.

You will join at the moment when the hard robotics questions become real product decisions: how do we turn customer needs into a highly capable robotic hand that is reliable, manufacturable, and ready to deploy on a real shop floor?

The Role

As Head of Product at TACTILIA, you will be the operational backbone of our product development. You will turn customer requirements into a robust roadmap — and the roadmap into a product that reaches the customer on time, on budget and at production quality.

You will lead through structure, clarity and commitment rather than hierarchy, and report to the CTO. You will work across product development, engineering and customer needs, keeping priorities aligned as TACTILIA moves from development towards production and scale.

What you will do

  • Own the product roadmap. Turn customer and market needs into clear product priorities and continuously balance customer value, engineering effort, technical risk, and time-to-market.

  • Turn requirements into product decisions. Work with Applications and customers to translate needs into clear, testable specifications, maintaining traceability from RFQ through validation.

  • Orchestrate product development. Coordinate Mechatronics, Software, Electronics, Systems Engineering and Applications across milestones, dependencies and interfaces, resolving conflicting priorities when needed.

  • Drive the product to production. Own development milestones, gate reviews, budget, unit cost and quality through to production readiness, while helping establish a scalable product development process.

  • Make the hard trade-offs. Bring together customer needs, technical feasibility, cost, quality and schedule to make pragmatic decisions and keep development moving.

  • Stay close to customers. Support the CTO in technical customer discussions, feasibility assessments, RFQs, trade fairs and partner conversations, bringing market feedback back into the product.

  • Build the organisation around the product. Identify gaps in capacity, skills and ownership across engineering, translate them into concrete hiring needs, and make pragmatic make-or-buy decisions.

  • Build for the real world. Work with engineering and operations to ensure the product is not only technically capable, but manufacturable, testable, reliable and ready to scale.

What you bring

  • A degree in Mechatronics, Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a comparable technical field.

  • 7+ years of experience developing complex mechatronic or hardware products, including significant experience in product development or technical project/programme management.

  • A proven track record taking products from requirements through development to production readiness.

  • Strong requirements management and a solid understanding of systems engineering.

  • Experience leading complex, multidisciplinary teams without direct line authority.

  • Strong product judgment and the ability to balance customer needs, technical feasibility, cost, quality and time-to-market.

  • A hands-on, structured approach and the ability to move between strategic decisions and day-to-day execution.

  • Fluent English; German is a strong plus.

Bonus

  • Experience in robotics, drive technology, gripping technology, or other highly integrated mechatronic systems.

title: Senior/Staff Software Engineer
description:
YOUR MISSION

 

A software engineer today uses Claude Code or Cursor. A mechanical engineer designing the next jet engine still searches Excel sheets and asks whoever has been around longest.

 

We are building the AI co-engineer for physical products: one that works natively in 3D and learns from real engineering decisions. We are in production with major European manufacturers, with real revenue and customers who tell us when we are slow.

 

The problems are open ones. Getting an agent to reason usefully about geometry, making 3D search work on real customer part libraries, and figuring out what the interface even looks like when an engineer asks why a bracket failed. There is research to borrow from and very little product to copy.

 

Senior or staff level depending on experience.

 

WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON

 

You will own large problems end to end, across the stack. We cannot say exactly what that looks like in month three, but here is what the last two years have actually involved.

 

  • A multi-agent orchestration SDK, built from scratch. Nothing off the shelf handled what we needed: long-horizon execution that runs for hours and survives restarts.

  • CAD conversion as a real pipeline. It used to be manual and brittle. Turning it into production infrastructure meant writing a Python wrapper around a C++ SDK and making it reliable enough to sit under everything else.

  • Migrating the application off Electron and Webpack onto SSR React with Vite. That architecture is what the whole product now sits on.

 

What is coming:

 

  • 3D-to-3D search across real customer part libraries, not benchmark datasets

  • Constraint solvers and optimization, and getting an agent to use one sensibly

  • Agents that hold a useful model of a physical object, which is still an open problem

  • Hybrid cloud deployments for manufacturers who cannot send their data anywhere

 

We work in Python and TypeScript, with multi-agent orchestration and AI integrations across several providers.

 

WHAT WE CARE ABOUT

 

  • You have shipped production systems across frontend and backend, and can point at them

  • Your CV reads as a set of problems, not a stack

  • You use AI heavily to go faster, but you built things the hard way first

  • You are fine when the problem is not yet defined

  • You deliver end to end, and you are still there when it needs maintaining

 

Bonus: CAD, computational geometry, constraint solving or optimization, 3D, LLM agents, industrial software. None required.

title: Founding Legal Engineer
description:
About Grubel

Grubel is a research lab that builds AI for high-stakes knowledge work, starting with law. Legal matters require specialized expertise, and each one involves its own facts, practices, parties, and institutions. General-purpose AI applies the same system to every legal matter, varying only what goes into a limited context window.

To meet the depth and diversity of legal work, we let every matter build its own AI: engineer the right data for the matter, adapt the model and agent to it, and track what improves. We combine the three into a matter-specific improvement loop that runs until the system delivers what the matter demands.

Grubel was founded in 2026 by Moritz Hardt, director at the Max Planck Institute for Intelligent Systems and formerly a UC Berkeley professor and Google Brain researcher; and Reinhard Heckel, professor of machine learning at the Technical University of Munich, on leave to build Grubel. The founding team includes engineers with PhDs in computer science and experience in foundation-model pretraining at Mistral and legal AI research at Thomson Reuters. The lab has offices in Munich and Tübingen.

Point Nine led an oversubscribed pre-seed funding round with backing from leading AI researchers and founders, including Jeff Dean, Chris Ré, Ion Stoica, and Harvey co-founders Gabe Pereyra and Winston Weinberg.


About the role

You are a skilled lawyer ideally with experience on building legal AI software eager to shape the technological future of your field. As a Founding Legal Engineer, you impact how we scope, build, and evaluate AI systems for complex legal work, and how these systems enter legal practice.

Working directly with Grubel’s founding team, you will shape our research, development, and product: Translate complex legal processes into agentic workflows, evaluate our systems for legal soundness and utility, and work with customers to set our product and engineering standards. You need not write code, but you’re passionate about understanding our technology deeply. Working in a fast-moving team at the intersection of AI research, legal practice, and technology excites you.

What you’ll work on

  • Designing realistic tasks, datasets, and evaluation rubrics for training and evaluation of our legal AI systems

  • Translating complex legal processes into agentic workflows together with our researchers and engineers

  • Evaluating system outputs for legal accuracy, usefulness, and failure modes

  • Leading enterprise pilots and implementations

  • Supporting customer discovery, demonstrations, and go-to-market initiatives

You may be a good fit if

  • You have law degree and strong academic record

  • You have experience practicing law—whether at a law firm, in-house, or in another legal setting

  • You are proactive, self-directed, and comfortable taking broad ownership at an early-stage company

  • You are curious about how AI systems work and comfortable working closely with researchers and engineers

Logistics

  • Munich or Tübingen. We value working together in person, prefer candidates based near one of our offices, and expect at least one day per week in the office. We plan to establish a Zurich office in 2027.

  • Full time employment

  • Competitive salary plus a stock option grant in Grubel, Inc., our US parent company.

title: Talent Acquisition Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Talent Acquisition Manager (m/w/d)

Du kennst den Unterschied zwischen einer geschalteten Anzeige und einer funktionierenden Recruiting-Strategie? Und du willst nicht nur eine Position im Haus besetzen, sondern die Personalgewinnung ganzer Unternehmen verantworten? Dann lies weiter.

Im klassischen Inhouse-Recruiting arbeitest du an den Stellen, die dir zugewiesen werden, mit dem Budget, das jemand anderes verhandelt hat. Bei uns läuft es umgekehrt: Du entscheidest, welche Unternehmen du gewinnst, wie ihre Recruiting-Strategie aussieht und über welche Kanäle die Besetzung läuft. Beratung, Umsetzung und Ergebnis liegen in einer Hand – deiner.

Aramaz Digital ist eine wachsende Recruiting-Beratung im Zentrum von Bielefeld. Wir machen Arbeitgeber sichtbar und liefern ihnen planbar passende Bewerbungen – über datengetriebene Kampagnen statt Zufallstreffer. Fachkräftemangel und demografische Entwicklung lassen diesen Markt jedes Jahr weiter wachsen.

Deine Verantwortung

Strategie und Beratung

  • Du analysierst, warum die Personalgewinnung eines Unternehmens nicht liefert – Zielgruppe, Positionierung, Kanäle, Prozessgeschwindigkeit.

  • Daraus entwickelst du eine belastbare Recruiting-Strategie und stellst sie den Entscheidern vor.

  • Du gewinnst neue Kunden aktiv: über Telefon, Direktansprache und Empfehlungen.

Kampagnen und Besetzung

  • Du planst Recruiting-Kampagnen, steuerst sie über die Laufzeit und justierst anhand der Zahlen nach.

  • Du prüfst eingehende Bewerbungen, führst Erstgespräche zur Vorauswahl und gestaltest eine Candidate Experience, die im Gedächtnis bleibt.

  • Bis zur erfolgreichen Besetzung bleibt das Projekt in deiner Hand.

Daten und Weiterentwicklung

  • Du arbeitest sauber im CRM, kennst deine Kennzahlen und leitest daraus konkrete Maßnahmen ab.

  • Gemeinsam mit Marketing und Geschäftsführung schärfst du unsere Methodik weiter.

Dein Profil

  • Recruiting-Verständnis: Du weißt, wie Zielgruppenansprache, Kanalauswahl und Prozessgestaltung zusammenwirken – ob aus Agentur, Personaldienstleistung oder Inhouse.

  • Beratungsstärke: Du triffst mit deinen Fragen den Kern, denkst in Lösungen und erklärst sie so, dass Entscheider mitgehen.

  • Vertriebsbereitschaft: Neue Kunden zu gewinnen gehört für dich dazu und schreckt dich nicht ab.

  • Zahlenaffinität: Du liest Kampagnendaten, erkennst Muster und handelst danach.

  • Eigenverantwortung: Du steuerst dich selbst, hältst nach Rückschlägen Kurs und misst dich an Ergebnissen.

  • Zum Hintergrund: Studium, Ausbildung oder Quereinstieg – wir schauen auf Können und Antrieb, nicht auf den Titel. Erfahrung im Recruiting ist willkommen, aber nichts, was wir dir nicht beibringen könnten.

Unser Angebot

  • Vergütung ohne Obergrenze: Fixgehalt als sichere Basis, dazu eine Provision, die nicht gedeckelt ist.

  • Unbefristet vom ersten Tag an: Wir planen langfristig – in einem Markt, der stabil wächst.

  • Klarer Entwicklungspfad: Recruiter, Junior Consultant, Senior Consultant. Das Tempo bestimmst du.

  • Einarbeitung mit Struktur: Umfassendes Onboarding, Trainings zu Recruiting, Beratung und Vertrieb, dazu feste Feedbackrunden.

  • Ausstattung auf Niveau: Höhenverstellbare Tische, Herman-Miller-Stühle, Apple-Hardware – mitten in der Bielefelder Innenstadt.

  • Fitness auf unsere Kosten: Premium-Mitgliedschaft im Studio deiner Wahl.

  • Gut versorgt: Siebträgerkaffee von Julius Meinl, ausgesuchte Tees, flexibles Mittagsangebot über Meyer Menü.

  • Flache Hierarchie: Leistungsorientiert und kollegial, mit direktem Draht zur Geschäftsführung.

Der Ablauf

  1. Bewerben in zwei Minuten – Lebenslauf genügt, kein Anschreiben nötig.

  2. Telefonat zum Kennenlernen – wir melden uns innerhalb von 48 Stunden.

  3. Persönliches Gespräch in unserem Büro in der Bielefelder Innenstadt.

Wenn du Recruiting nicht abarbeiten, sondern gestalten willst: Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung.

description:
As a Senior Prototyping Engineer – Thermal Systems & Cooling Integration, you will become an integral part of our Prototyping team, supporting the development of our Reliant platform – a next-generation long-range eVTOL unmanned aerial system designed for demanding ISR and logistics missions. Reliant combines exceptional endurance, modularity, and operational flexibility to deliver mission-critical capabilities in the most challenging environments.

In this role, you will be responsible for the integration, development, and validation of thermal management and cooling systems for the aircraft. You will develop efficient cooling concepts for hybrid propulsion components, power electronics, avionics, and other heat-generating systems by optimizing airflow, aerodynamic cooling, and thermal integration. Working closely with mechanical, propulsion, and systems engineering teams, you will ensure reliable operation across demanding flight and environmental conditions.


What is your Day to Day Mission:

  • Lead the integration and development of thermal management and cooling systems for UAVs.

  • Design and optimize cooling concepts for combustion engines, generators, power electronics, avionics, and other onboard systems.

  • Design, build, and commission prototype cooling test rigs and instrumentation for system validation.

title: Founding GTM Engineer
description:
Your responsibilities

We're looking for Plato's first GTM Engineer: the person who brings RevOps to Plato as a discipline and builds our revenue engine as a product, not a ticket queue. Pipeline, conversion, and revenue per headcount are your metrics.
You're inheriting real infrastructure - HubSpot as our source of truth, a custom-built deal-scoring app, call intelligence via Grain, and company-wide AI access - but the layers underneath are still unbuilt: clean data, automated process, real forecasting rigor, AI-driven workflows. That's the job.
This is a team-of-one role that's essentially a sandbox: a direct line to the founders, a mandate to change how we work, and no playbook telling you what to build first. If you want to build the infrastructure behind a revenue engine from the ground up and see your own builds move real numbers, let's talk.

What you'll actually do:

  • Get the data foundation trustworthy: CRM hygiene, field governance, deduping, enrichment on create
  • Automate the revenue process: lead routing, SLAs, stage criteria, clean handoffs across teams
  • Build the pipeline generation stack: signal-based outbound (ICP scoring, enrichment waterfalls, orchestration) so effort goes into conversations, not list-building
  • Bring AI into daily workflows: call-intelligence automation, research agents, health/churn scoring
  • Get forecasting and reporting to a place leadership can steer from weekly
  • Make sure what you ship gets used: instrument adoption, train the team, iterate


Your qualifications

Must-haves:

  • Hands-on experience architecting a CRM like HubSpot from the ground up - how objects, properties, and data structure are set up - not just administering one that's already built
  • Practical, production experience with outbound/enrichment tooling (e.g. Clay or similar)
  • You've built with AI/LLMs - prompt design, agents, or AI-powered workflows - in real production work
  • Strong data rigor: you can read a funnel, spot where the data is dirty, and quantify the impact of a fix before you build it
  • You think in systems and sequencing, not tickets - and can defend your reasoning under real pushback

Nice-to-haves:
  • Experience as an early GTM-Ops/RevOps hire at another startup
  • Familiarity with our stack or similar: Grain, Sales Navigator-style outbound tooling
  • Comfort with unit economics (CAC, ACV, payback)
  • Experience with mid-market, multi-stakeholder B2B deal cycles


Why us?

You'd be Plato's first-ever GTM Engineer - not inheriting someone else's system, but building the one that doesn't exist yet, and introducing RevOps as a discipline at a company that's never had one. A direct line to the founders, real budget for tooling, and a mandate to change how the revenue team works, from day one. 
This is an individual contributor role today - you'll be doing the building yourself, not managing a team. If this function grows as Plato scales, you'd be the one shaping what it becomes, not stepping into a structure someone else already defined.
Because the function touches everything - data, process, automation, AI - you won't be boxed into one lane. If you want to see your own build move a real number within your first 90 days, this is that role.

title: Cloud Platform Engineer (m/w/d)
description:
Ab

sofort


Das erwartet dich

Wir bauen mit unserem Green-Field-Ansatz eine neue Cloud in unseren deutschen Rechenzentren auf — vollständig selbst gehostet, cloud-native und ohne Abhängigkeit von amerikanischen Hyperscalern. Jeder unserer Kunden erhält ein dediziertes Kubernetes-Cluster auf Basis des SUSE-Stacks (Harvester, RKE2), ausgerollt und verwaltet über Fleet, mit eigenem Tenant-Management.

Du bist nicht Betreiber eines fremden Systems, sondern gestaltest die Plattform, auf der unsere Software als SaaS läuft — mit echter Verantwortung und echtem Gestaltungsspielraum.

Digitale Souveränität ist bei uns kein Versprechen, sondern Betriebsrealität. Auf dieser Plattform laufen die geschäftskritischen Anwendungen von Versicherern und Auftraggebern der öffentlichen Hand. Die Anforderungen an Verfügbarkeit, Informationssicherheit und Nachweisbarkeit sind auf allerhöchsten Level. Hierfür sind unsere Managed Services nach BSI C5 testiert.

Das erwartet dich

Plattform entwickeln und gestalten

  • Konzeption, Aufbau und Weiterentwicklung der selbst gehosteten Cloud-Plattform (Multi-Cluster, ohne Hyperscaler-Abhängigkeit, volle Kontrolle)
  • Architektur und Design hochverfügbarer Kubernetes-Cluster im SUSE-Stack, inklusive Networking, Storage, Load Balancing und Authentifizierung
  • Design und Weiterentwicklung des Tenant-Konzepts: isolierte Kundenumgebungen, Verantwortung für Architektur und Lifecycle
  • Abstimmung mit der Entwicklung zu performance- und verfügbarkeitsrelevanten Anforderungen an das Cluster- und Tenant-Konzept
  • Weiterentwicklung des Hochverfügbarkeitskonzepts: Ein verteilter In-Memory Ansatz über mehrere Knoten (Schwarmtechnik), der die Echtzeitfähigkeit der Anwendungen im Normalbetrieb sicherstellt
Automatisieren und standardisieren
  • GitOps-Workflows über ArgoCD und Fleet — von der Erstauslieferung bis zum Day-2-Betrieb vollständig automatisiert
  • Infrastructure as Code mit Ansible, Terraform oder vergleichbaren Tools; Policy as Code für Sicherheit und Governance
  • CI/CD-Integration und Standardisierung der Deployment-Prozesse
Brücke zu den Entwicklungsteams und Kunden
  • Platform Engineering für interne Teams: Aufbau von Self-Service-Fähigkeiten, Definition von Standards, Begleitung des Onboardings
  • Aktive Unterstützung der Entwicklungsteams bei der Migration ihrer Workloads in die Cloud-Plattform
  • Verarbeitung von Erkenntnissen aus dem laufenden Betrieb (Monitoring-Daten, Incidents) zur kontinuierlichen Weiterentwicklung von Stabilität, Sicherheit und Performance


Das bringst du mit

Must-have

  • Mehrjährige Erfahrung im Cloud- oder Platform-Engineering, in Container-Technologien oder Infrastrukturautomatisierung
  • Fundierte Kubernetes Kenntnisse, idealerweise aus dem Betrieb produktiver Multi-Cluster-Umgebungen
  • Erfahrung mit GitOps-Workflows (idealerweise ArgoCD oder Fleet) und Infrastructure as Code (z. B. Ansible, Terraform)
  • Verhandlungssichere Deutschkenntnisse (mind. C1) sowie sehr gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift
  • Reisebereitschaft für Kundentermine und Termine an unseren weiteren Standorten
Nice-to-have
  • Erfahrung mit SUSE Stack oder vergleichbaren Kubernetes-Management-Plattformen
  • Kenntnisse in DevSecOps, Policy as Code oder Hochverfügbarkeitskonzepten
  • Erfahrung mit Monitoring-Stacks (z. B. Prometheus, Grafana)
Persönlich
  • Systemisches Denken statt Ticket-Fokus, mit Blick fürs Gesamtbild
  • Sicheres Auftreten und Kommunikation auf Augenhöhe mit Entwicklungsteams wie mit Kunden
  • Strukturierte, eigenständige und lösungsorientierte Arbeitsweise
  • Erfahrung darin, Themen über Team- und Kundengrenzen hinweg zu steuern


Was wir dir bieten

  • Übernimm Verantwortung und nutze deinen Gestaltungsspielraum, um eigene Ideen zu verwirklichen.
  • Arbeite dort, wo Wirkung entsteht: im Office oder direkt beim Kunden. Homeoffice ist die Ausnahme – dafür bieten wir dir flexible Arbeitszeiten und ein Office, in dem man gerne arbeitet und den Tag gemeinsam verbringt.
  • Profitiere von internen und externen Schulungen, die dich fachlich und persönlich weiterbringen.
  • Genieße Benefits wie BusinessBike, EGYM Wellpass, Corporate Benefits und einen Zuschuss für den ÖPNV.
  • Neben einem VWL-Zuschuss bieten wir dir eine betriebliche Altersvorsorge und eine Kita-Förderung.
  • Ob Surfen, Wandern, Mountainbiken oder Golfen – bei unseren vielseitigen Mitarbeiter-Events ist für jeden etwas dabei!

description:
Warum LPE Immobilien?

  • Die Hausverwaltung ist der unterschätzteste Beruf Deutschlands: Kein anderer entscheidet so unmittelbar darüber, wie Menschen wohnen. Trotzdem gilt der Hausverwalter bis heute als Buchhalter mit Schlüsselbund. Wir wollen das ändern, und Software ist dafür einer unserer zentralen Hebel.
  • Mit lpeOS bauen wir die Systeme, mit denen wir selbst jeden Tag arbeiten: das Kundenportal für unsere Eigentümer, KI-Agenten, die eigenständig Aufgaben übernehmen, und das Verwaltercockpit als Arbeitsumgebung unserer Verwalter. Wir digitalisieren unsere eigenen Prozesse, um die Arbeit unserer Verwalter jeden Tag ein Stück besser zu machen, mit dem Anspruch, die Branche zu revolutionieren.
  • Kaum eine Branche wurde von moderner Software so lange übersehen. Der Abstand zwischen dem, was ist, und dem, was möglich ist, ist riesig, und wir bauen ihn Stück für Stück zu. Du wärst eine der ersten Personen im Produktteam.


Was dich bei uns erwartet – Deine Aufgaben

  • Du entwickelst Fullstack in TypeScript, vom Kundenportal über das Verwaltercockpit bis zu den Services und der Infrastruktur dahinter, auf der grünen Wiese und ohne Altlasten. Features verantwortest du end-to-end: von der Idee über die Gestaltung bis zum Release, bei Bedarf auch ohne Designer an deiner Seite.
  • Du baust KI-Agenten als Produktfunktionalität für unsere Verwalter und Kunden. Zugleich entwickeln wir unsere eigene Entwicklungsumgebung permanent weiter: ein modernes Setup rund um Cursor und Claude Code, inklusive Agent-Graph-Loops und Harness.
  • Dabei arbeitest du nah an den Nutzern: Deine Kolleginnen, Kollegen und Kunden sind direkt erreichbar, Feedback bekommst du auf kurzem und direktem Weg. Wir sammeln Probleme, bewerten sie und bauen die wichtigsten in festen Cycles.
  • Unser Stack: TypeScript durchgehend, mit React und Next.js im Frontend und Node im Backend, als Monorepo auf Google Cloud (Infrastructure as Code), dazu Postgres und event-getriebene Prozesse. Du musst nicht alles davon kennen, den Rest lernst du bei uns.


Was du mitbringen solltest

  • 2 bis 4 Jahre Erfahrung in der Webentwicklung.
  • Sichere Praxis in TypeScript oder JavaScript, idealerweise mit React oder Next.js.
  • Ein aktuelles Projekt, das du zeigen kannst: Produktionscode, Side Project oder Open Source.
  • Du arbeitest gern quer über den ganzen Stack und magst Frontend und Backend ähnlich gern.
  • Du verantwortest Features end-to-end und kannst bei Bedarf auch ohne Designer ein gutes Interface gestalten.
  • KI-Tooling ist Teil deines Arbeitsalltags, und du prüfst die Ergebnisse genauso kritisch, wie du sie nutzt.
  • Grundverständnis von Datenbanken (SQL) und API-Design.
  • Du willst verstehen, warum etwas gebaut wird, bevor du es baust.
  • Deutschkenntnisse mindestens auf B2-Niveau.
Du erfüllst nicht alle Punkte? Bewirb dich trotzdem. Talent und Lernkurve zählen bei uns mehr als Jahreszahlen im Lebenslauf.


Was wir dir bieten

  • Eine seltene Ausgangslage. Wir bauen Software für ein Geschäftsmodell, das bereits funktioniert, und wissen, dass sie gebraucht wird. Du erlebst aus nächster Nähe, wie sich eine ganze Branche neu erfindet, und gestaltest das aktiv mit.
  • Echter Impact. Alles, was du baust, kommt bei unseren Verwaltern, Eigentümern und Kunden direkt zum Einsatz.
  • Eine Branche von innen kennenlernen. Die Immobilienwirtschaft ist einer der größten Märkte Deutschlands und steht erst am Anfang ihrer Digitalisierung. Du lernst sie dort kennen, wo die Entscheidungen fallen.
  • Direkte Zusammenarbeit mit den Produktverantwortlichen. Kurze Wege, schnelle Entscheidungen und jemand, der sich Zeit für deine Fragen nimmt.

  • Die richtigen Werkzeuge. Premium-Hardware, cloudbasierte Tools, aktuelles KI-Tooling, papierlos. Wenn dir etwas fehlt, um besser zu arbeiten, bekommst du es.

title: Product Manager – Android Integration & Ecosystem
description:
Your mission

As our Product Manager – Android Integration & Ecosystem, you will define the product what and why for how ProGlove devices connect, integrate and create value within the enterprise Android ecosystem.

ProGlove is evolving from a wearable scanner company into a Worker Companion company, bringing together ergonomic wearable hardware, software, connectivity, workflow guidance, data and intelligence. With the MAI Wearable Companion, we are entering a broader ecosystem of enterprise applications, technologies, standards, partners and customer infrastructure.

Your mission will be to make our products easy to adopt, integrate and deploy at scale – without turning every customer opportunity into a bespoke engineering project. You will identify recurring customer needs, translate them into scalable capabilities and propositions, and decide where ProGlove should own, enable or partner. In doing so, you will help turn integration from a technical necessity into a source of differentiation, customer value and commercial opportunity.

You will work closely with the Product Manager responsible for the Wearable Companion device. While they own the device proposition, you will own how the device connects to and creates value in the wider ecosystem. Together, you will shape a coherent end-to-end proposition for customers, developers, integrators and partners.

Your day-to-day 
  • Define and evolve the product strategy and priorities for ProGlove’s enterprise Android integration and ecosystem capabilities, aligned with customer needs and business goals.
  • Work directly with customers, Sales and Solution Architecture to identify recurring problems, distinguish individual requests from broader market needs and turn the right opportunities into scalable solutions.
  • Translate recurring integration needs into repeatable product capabilities such as APIs, SDKs, tools, interfaces, documentation, integration patterns and deployment solutions.
  • Shape the product experience around device setup, provisioning, application distribution, device management and other capabilities required to deploy and operate connected device fleets at scale.
  • Make clear, pragmatic decisions about where ProGlove should own, enable or partner, balancing customer value, strategic control, speed, scalability and technical complexity.
  • Identify the platforms, applications, standards and ecosystem players that matter to our customers, and shape the integrations, certifications and technology partnerships that strengthen our proposition.
  • Explore where integration capabilities, software, services and ecosystem propositions can create differentiated value and support commercial or recurring-revenue opportunities.
  • Partner closely with Engineering and the Product Manager for the Wearable Companion to create alignment on customer problems, priorities, trade-offs and desired outcomes.
  • Enable Sales and other customer-facing teams to clearly explain our Android proposition, supported capabilities, integrations and common deployment patterns.
  • Maintain a forward-looking view of enterprise Android, AOSP, enterprise mobility, AI and adjacent technologies, and translate relevant developments into strategic options and product priorities.


Your profile

At ProGlove, technical expertise matters, but how you work is just as important. We are looking for someone who takes ownership, stays curious, collaborates openly and turns complexity into clear, pragmatic decisions.

  • You bring strong Product Management experience in B2B or enterprise technology and can define strategy, discover meaningful customer problems, prioritize opportunities and turn them into scalable products or propositions.
  • You are commercially minded and naturally connect product decisions with customer value, differentiation, business impact and opportunities to capture value.
  • You are comfortable working with enterprise software, platforms, connected devices, integrations or technology ecosystems, and understand the realities of complex customer IT environments.
  • You have enough technical depth to understand architecture, interfaces and trade-offs, contribute credibly to platform and integration discussions, and recognize when deeper engineering expertise is needed.
  • You think in systems and patterns: when faced with a customer requirement, you look beyond the immediate request to understand why it exists, how broadly it applies and what a simple, repeatable solution could look like.
  • You take end-to-end ownership, move topics forward without waiting for perfect instructions and remain effective when the product space or path ahead is not yet fully defined.
  • You collaborate generously and build trust across Product, Engineering, Sales, Solution Architecture, customers and external partners. You can create alignment and drive decisions without relying on formal authority.
  • You communicate clearly and transparently, raise risks early and can make complex technical and commercial topics understandable to different audiences.
  • You are curious about customers, the business and emerging technologies, and continuously test assumptions rather than pursuing technology for its own sake.
  • You use pragmatic judgment to balance speed, simplicity, quality and long-term value.
  • You are fluent in English and comfortable working in an international environment.

Experience in one or more of the following areas would be valuable, but is not required:

  • Enterprise Android, AOSP or adjacent Android ecosystems, including environments operating outside standard Google Mobile Services.
  • Enterprise mobility management, MDM/EMM, device provisioning, application deployment or connected fleet management.
  • Rugged or industrial devices, IoT or edge devices, connected hardware or other B2B technology ecosystems.
  • APIs, SDKs, developer or integrator experiences and enterprise integrations.
  • Platform or ecosystem strategy, technology partnerships, certification programs or developer and partner ecosystems.
  • Enterprise customers deploying technology at scale.
Direct Android Product Management experience is an advantage, but not essential if you bring strong Product Management expertise and relevant experience from an adjacent enterprise technology ecosystem.


Why us?

This is an opportunity to shape an important part of a category that is still being defined. 
Android gives ProGlove access to a much broader technology ecosystem, but the opportunity goes far beyond compatibility. You will help determine what role ProGlove should play in that ecosystem, which capabilities we should own, where we should partner, what customers and developers should be able to build around us, and where integration itself can become a source of differentiation and recurring business value. 
ProGlove already has the customer base, market credibility, technology and industrial expertise to build on. Our products are used in some of the world's most demanding operational environments. What we are now building is the next layer. 
Over time, success will mean more than making our own products easier to integrate. It will mean creating capabilities, interfaces and ecosystem relationships that customers, application providers and partners actively choose to build around - moving ProGlove from ecosystem participant toward ecosystem shaper. 
If you are excited by the idea of turning complex technology ecosystems into simple, valuable products - and helping shape how the next generation of frontline technology connects with the digital world - we would love to meet you. 
Join us in building the future of frontline work.


What success looks like

  • ProGlove has a clear, customer-backed strategy and prioritized roadmap for Android integration and ecosystem capabilities.
  • Recurring customer and integration needs are turned into scalable, repeatable solutions rather than one-off engineering projects.
  • Customers can adopt, integrate, deploy and manage ProGlove devices more easily within their existing enterprise environments.
  • Decisions about what ProGlove should own, enable or partner are made transparently and based on customer value, business impact and long-term scalability.
  • Product, Engineering, Sales and Solution Architecture are aligned on priorities, supported capabilities and key trade-offs.
  • Customer-facing teams can confidently communicate our Android proposition and common deployment patterns without relying on Product or Engineering in every opportunity.
  • Relevant integrations, partnerships and commercial opportunities are identified, validated and translated into tangible product or business outcomes.


Meet your team

You will join our Product team and report directly to the CPO. You will work especially closely with the Product Manager responsible for the Wearable Companion, as well as colleagues across Engineering, Sales, Solution Architecture and Product Marketing.

This is a highly cross-functional role. You will bring together customer needs, technical realities and commercial opportunities, while also building relationships with external technology partners, platform providers and integrators. The team values open collaboration, clear communication and shared ownership of outcomes.

title: AI Platform Working Student
description:
About CHAPTERS Group

CHAPTERS Group AG is a Hamburg-based holding company investing in 55+ mission-critical software companies across the DACH region, France, and the Czech Republic. Our companies deliver the digital solutions that keep the public sector and core industries running. What they do matters in daily life.

AI has rapidly disrupted the software industry, and we aim to lead that transformation across our portfolio. Central to this is the AI Core team: we build and operate a shared enterprise AI Hub used by companies across the group, and drive adoption through a network of AI Champions. Each portfolio company has one designated power user who leads AI enablement locally, runs training, and scales usage within their organisation.

Tasks

The Role

You will work as a full member of the AI Core team, supporting the infrastructure that powers AI adoption across 55+ portfolio companies. The team's core product is the AI Hub platform (Open WebUI): we keep it running, deploy new instances, build and validate integrations, and ensure every company in the group has a stable, well-configured environment.

We build the AI Hub as a product and ship it to every company in the portfolio. Each company owns and administers their own Hub (L1 Support). The AI Core team drives the features, changes, and integrations that create value across all hubs and serves as the centre of expertise (L2 Support) when local teams need guidance or hands-on help.

You will have direct ownership of tasks, contribute your own ideas, and actively shape how the platform evolves. This is not an observation role, you will work on the same codebase and infrastructure as the rest of the team.

What You Will Work On

  • Deploy, configure, and maintain shared AI Hub instances across Azure and AWS
  • Build and test platform tools, functions, and custom AI agents based on specifications
  • Monitor platform health, uptime, logs, and configuration consistency across all deployed AI Hub instances
  • Build health-check, alerting, and reporting scripts that track version parity, uptime, cloud usage, and deployment status
  • Support containerized application deployment, environment configuration, secrets handling, and rollback processes
  • Implement and validate integrations with infrastructure and enterprise services such as MCP servers, Git/Bitbucket, Microsoft Graph, and data providers
  • Write deployment guides, runbooks, and onboarding documentation for new companies joining the platform
  • Monitor core platform and dependency releases, then summarize operational impact, upgrade steps, and risks for the group

Requirements

What We Are Looking For

Required

  • Currently enrolled in a Master's program in Computer Science, Data Science, AI/ML, Software Engineering, or related field
  • Strong Python skills, comfortable writing scripts, calling APIs, and building small applications
  • Comfortable with Bash/shell scripting and working in a Linux terminal
  • Basic familiarity with cloud infrastructure and application deployment on Azure or AWS
  • Practical experience using LLMs via API (OpenAI, Anthropic, or similar)
  • Familiarity with Docker, REST APIs, Git, and deployment workflows
  • Ability to read and work from technical documentation independently
  • Strong written communication in English (fluent) and German (fluent)

Bonus

  • Cloud platform certifications in Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud are a plus, especially when paired with hands-on deployment or operations experience
  • Experience with cloud application platforms, LangChain, LlamaIndex, or agentic AI frameworks
  • Infrastructure as Code awareness (Bicep, Terraform, CloudFormation)
  • Familiarity with authentication concepts (OAuth, SSO, JWT)
  • Experience with monitoring, logging, or cloud operations tools such as Azure Monitor or CloudWatch

Benefits

What You'll Get

  • Work on infrastructure and tooling that directly shapes how 55+ software companies adopt AI, your output has immediate, visible impact across the group
  • Become part of CHAPTERS Group, a German serial acquirer with 10x growth in the past five years and high ambitions for what comes next
  • Full integration into the AI Core team, contributing alongside senior engineers from day one, with a direct line to the CTO office
  • Hands-on experience building, deploying, and maintaining enterprise AI infrastructure across Azure and AWS in production
  • Access to enterprise AI tooling: Claude Code, Azure OpenAI, and a modern multi-cloud AI platform stack
  • Direct ownership of tasks with measurable impact, not support work or observation
  • Active investment in your development: mentorship from the AI Core team, exposure to real architecture decisions, and access to relevant events and conferences

How to Apply

Send your CV along with a brief note on why this role interests you and what you would bring to the AI Core team. No formal cover letter required.

We are looking forward to your application!

title: Service- & Vertriebsassistenz (m/w/d): Organisationstalent mit Anpacker-Mentalität
description:
Vielleicht suchen wir genau dich.

Denn ganz ehrlich:
Wenn du einfach nur einen Job suchst, um irgendwo deine Stunden abzusitzen, sind wir wahrscheinlich nicht füreinander gemacht.

Wenn du aber denkst:

„Ich kann mehr. Ich will mehr. Und ich möchte zeigen, was ich kann.“

… dann wird es interessant.

Wir sind ein familiengeführtes Autohaus in Leer und vertreten die Marken Toyota und Mitsubishi. Bei uns arbeiten Verkauf, Service und Werkstatt eng zusammen – und genau an dieser Schnittstelle suchen wir Verstärkung.

Als Service- & Vertriebsassistenz bist du eine wichtige Schnittstelle zwischen unseren Kunden, der Werkstatt, dem Verkauf und dem restlichen Team.

  • Du bist persönlich, telefonisch und per E-Mail eine der ersten Anlaufstellen für unsere Kunden.

  • Du unterstützt bei der Vorbereitung, Bearbeitung und Nachbereitung von Werkstattaufträgen.

Vertriebsunterstützung

  • Du begleitest Neu- und Gebrauchtfahrzeuge organisatorisch von der Hereinnahme bis zur Auslieferung.

  • Du kümmerst dich um notwendige Hersteller- und Prämienmeldungen und behältst dabei Fristen im Blick.

Und sonst?
Du siehst, wenn etwas fehlt oder nicht funktioniert, und wartest nicht darauf, dass jemand anderes es irgendwann bemerkt. Ordnung, Material, Abläufe und ein gepflegter Kundenbereich gehören für uns genauso zu einem gut funktionierenden Autohaus wie Telefon und Computer.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

Du musst bei uns nicht perfekt sein. Du musst auch nicht vom ersten Tag an alles können.

Aber du solltest Lust haben, Dinge anzupacken.

Du übernimmst Verantwortung, ohne dass ständig jemand hinter dir stehen muss. Du bist freundlich und offen – nicht nur, wenn gerade jemand zuschaut. Du hast dieses gewisse „Ich-kümmere-mich-darum“-Gen. Du kannst mehrere Bälle gleichzeitig in der Luft halten, ohne dabei den Überblick zu verlieren.

Du arbeitest sorgfältig und zuverlässig.
Gründlich? Ja. Pedantisch? Bitte nicht.

Und wenn etwas mal nicht funktioniert, suchst du nicht zuerst jemanden, dem du die Schuld geben kannst. Du suchst eine Lösung.

Erfahrung im Autohaus, im Service oder im kaufmännischen Bereich ist natürlich von Vorteil. Noch wichtiger sind uns aber deine Einstellung, dein Organisationstalent und die Bereitschaft, Neues zu lernen.

Benefits

Das bekommst du von uns

Vertrauen. Verantwortung. Freiraum.

Und die Möglichkeit, wirklich etwas zu bewegen. Wir wollen niemanden, der einfach nur eine Stelle ausfüllt. Wir wollen jemanden, der seinen Platz mitgestaltet.

Jemanden, bei dem wir nach ein paar Monaten sagen: „Gut, dass wir genau dich gefunden haben.“

Und vielleicht sagst du dann: „Gut, dass ich mich getraut habe.“

Also – wer bist du?

Wenn du dich jetzt ein bisschen ertappt fühlst, sollten wir uns kennenlernen.

Kein Bewerbungsmarathon. Kein Verhör. Kein „Wo sehen Sie sich in fünf Jahren?“.

Lass uns einfach miteinander reden.

Vielleicht passt es. Vielleicht sogar ziemlich gut.

Wir suchen nicht.

Wir finden.

Und vielleicht bist du genau die Person, die wir finden wollen.

title: Firmware Engineer

Our product — termios Pro — replaces standard radiator thermostats in existing buildings, performs hydraulic balancing via a self-learning algorithm, and cuts heating energy consumption by up to 30%. No battery, no retrofitting: the device harvests energy from the temperature differential between radiator and room air (thermo-harvesting) and communicates over LoRaWAN.

The system runs at scale across multi-unit residential portfolios. Each thermostat is a constrained embedded device operating autonomously, syncing state through a LoRaWAN gateway to a cloud backend that runs the optimization logic. title: VP Finance
description:
The Role

We are seeking a VP Finance to build the finance function that will support Geordie through its next stage of growth.

Your mission is to build the financial foundation that enables Geordie to scale with confidence. You'll combine rigorous financial management, thoughtful planning and modern systems to give the business the insight, discipline and operational excellence it needs to grow.

Initially, you will be a hands-on individual contributor responsible for building and operating the finance function. You'll own financial planning, reporting, forecasting, cash management and financial operations, while working closely with our external finance partners who manage bookkeeping, VAT and other compliance processes.

This is not a traditional finance role focused solely on reporting historical numbers. We are looking for someone who enjoys building systems, improving processes and helping leadership make better decisions through high-quality financial analysis and insight.

Over time, you'll build an exceptionally efficient finance function that leverages automation and AI wherever practical, allowing the team to scale alongside the business without growing linearly with headcount.

What You'll Do

Financial Leadership

  • Own the finance function end-to-end, initially as Geordie's sole internal finance hire.

  • Build robust financial planning, budgeting and forecasting processes that support rapid company growth.

  • Own the company operating model, including revenue, ARR, hiring plans, cash runway and scenario modelling.

  • Produce clear, high-quality reporting for leadership, the Board and investors.

  • Partner closely with the CEO and leadership team to provide financial analysis that supports strategic decision-making.

Financial Operations

  • Own cash flow management, treasury oversight and working capital.

  • Oversee invoicing, accounts payable and financial operations, working closely with external finance partners.

  • Build scalable quote-to-cash processes alongside RevOps and Legal, ensuring strong financial controls as the business grows.

  • Ensure banking, insurance and core financial infrastructure operate effectively.

  • Own financial compliance across our UK and US entities, including tax requirements, R&D claims and coordination with external advisers.

Business Performance

  • Develop a deep understanding of the company's unit economics, gross margins and customer profitability.

  • Help leadership understand where capital is being deployed most effectively and provide financial insight to support investment decisions.

  • Support commercial teams with financial analysis around customer profitability, pricing, commercial structures and larger customer opportunities.

  • Partner with Product as a finance domain expert, providing input into the evolution of Geordie's cost management capabilities.

Finance Systems & Automation

  • Help build a modern, highly efficient finance function through thoughtful use of AI, automation and best-in-class financial systems.

  • Work closely with our Internal Systems & AI Lead to identify opportunities to automate finance workflows, improve reporting and reduce manual effort.

  • Continuously improve finance systems, processes and controls to increase the leverage of the finance function as the company scales.

Fundraising & Growth

  • Support future fundraising processes through financial modelling, investor reporting and due diligence.

  • Help ensure the business maintains the financial discipline and operational maturity required to scale.

  • Over time, build and lead a lean, high-performing finance team as the complexity of the business grows.

Ideal Background

  • Experience leading finance within a high-growth B2B SaaS or technology company.

  • Strong background in FP&A, strategic finance or commercial finance, with the ability to build robust financial models and planning processes.

  • Comfortable operating as a hands-on individual contributor while building functions from first principles.

  • Experience producing Board and investor reporting and supporting fundraising or due diligence processes.

  • Strong commercial acumen with the ability to translate financial data into actionable business insight.

  • Experience improving finance systems, processes and operational workflows.

  • Curious about AI and excited by the opportunity to build a modern, highly automated finance function.

  • Highly proactive, organised and comfortable operating independently in a fast-moving environment.

Why This Role

Finance has an opportunity to change dramatically over the coming decade. We believe AI and automation will fundamentally change how finance teams operate, allowing small teams to deliver far greater leverage than ever before.

At Geordie, we want to build a finance function that embraces that opportunity from day one. Rather than scaling through headcount alone, we want to scale through better systems, better automation and better decision-making.

This role offers the opportunity to build that function from the ground up and, over time, grow it into a world-class finance organisation while helping shape the future of one of the fastest-growing AI security companies.

Our Values

Solve What Matters

We listen intently and stay focused on what truly matters to our customers. If it doesn't help them navigate real-world agentic adoption and risk, it's probably not worth building.

Build, Learn, Iterate

We favour momentum over perfection; testing, learning, and evolving through action. It's how we move fast and get better, together.

Kind, Not Comfortable

We're honest, respectful, and unafraid to challenge each other. We believe doing great work should feel good, too. Kindness makes that possible.
